title: The Blue Roller
author: Ilse Marchetti
hook: A dead bird, a stolen painting, and the summer a family finally told the truth.
blurb:
In 1583 a painter laid a blue roller on his table and drew it feather by feather. Four centuries later the drawing hangs in Lena Moretti's hallway, and no one in the family will say how it got there.
When her father dies and the museum comes asking, Lena must decide what she owes the living, the dead, and the bird that has watched them all.
bio: Ilse Marchetti grew up between Trieste and Leeds. Her stories have appeared in literary journals on three continents. She lives by the sea with a printmaker and too many books.

title: The Bridge in the Rain
author: Kenji Arai
hook: One bridge. One sudden shower. Three strangers who will never forget each other.
blurb:
Tokyo, an ordinary Tuesday. A widowed carpenter, a schoolgirl running from an exam and a translator with a letter she cannot send all take shelter under the same umbrella.
Told across the eleven minutes the rain lasts, this is a quiet, luminous novel about the small mercies that change a life without anyone noticing.
bio: Kenji Arai writes in Japanese and English. He worked as a bridge engineer for twenty years before turning to fiction. He lives in Kamakura.

title: The Linen Year
author: Nell Ashworth
hook: Some summers bleach everything they touch. Even the truth.
blurb:
In the year the priory washing line went up, Agnes was nine and her mother stopped speaking to God.
Twelve months, twelve linens, one village that keeps its secrets folded and pressed. A tender, sharp-eyed debut about faith, laundry and the women who hold a place together while the men argue about it.
bio: Nell Ashworth was born in a Cotswold village not unlike this one. She teaches creative writing and keeps bees, badly.

title: The Tide Tables
author: Agathe Varga
tagline: Every summer the sea gave something back.
hook: Every summer the sea gave something back.
blurb:
For forty years Odile has walked the shore at Pourville at low tide. A shoe. A wedding ring. A message in a bottle written in her own hand.
Now the sea has returned her brother, missing since 1962, and the village wants answers she has spent a lifetime avoiding. A novel of grief, weather and second chances.
bio: Agathe Varga is a French-Hungarian novelist and former oceanographer. This is her third novel.

title: Soft Animals
author: Mina Okafor
hook: You do not have to be good.
blurb:
Ada has been good all her life: the good daughter, the good wife, the good nurse. Then, at fifty-two, she buys an orchard nobody wants and stops answering the phone.
A warm, funny and fierce novel about the second half of a woman's life, and the apple that starts it.
bio: Mina Okafor is a Nigerian-British writer and former paediatric nurse. She lives in Kent, among apple trees.

title: A Season of Tulips
author: Eleanor Vance
hook: Haarlem, 1636. Every bulb is worth a fortune. So is her heart.
blurb:
Clara de Witt has one season to save her father's debts, and one rare bulb to do it with. Pieter Vos, the city's most ruthless trader, has the money to buy it.
The price he asks is not in guilders. Lush, witty and swoon-worthy, the first of The Haarlem Brides.
bio: Eleanor Vance writes historical romance with a taste for hothouses, ledgers and impossible men. She lives in Norfolk with a greenhouse full of tulips.

title: Seen at 2:14
author: Hattie Bloom
tagline: He left her on read. Then he moved in next door.
hook: He left her on read. Then he moved in next door.
blurb:
Juno sent one honest text at 2:14 a.m. Ezra saw it. Ezra never replied.
Three years later he is her new neighbour, her landlord's nephew and the only man in London who can fix her boiler. She would rather freeze. A sparkling, laugh-out-loud romance about second chances and very thin walls.
bio: Hattie Bloom writes romantic comedies between shifts at a bookshop. She has never left anyone on read. Probably.

title: A Vow of Silver Moons
author: Isolde Varga
hook: Three moons. One vow. A crown that drinks the tide.
blurb:
In the Tidecourt, every bride is promised to the sea. Marin was meant to drown at dawn. Instead the sea sent her back with silver in her veins, and the cruel prince who swore to wed her now swears to break her.
An enemies-to-lovers romantasy of storm, salt and impossible choices.
bio: Isolde Varga writes romantic fantasy by lamplight on the Cornish coast. A Vow of Silver Moons is her first novel.

title: The Devil's Vow
author: Sienna Vale
hook: He kept every promise. That was the problem.
blurb:
Sienna owes the Moretti family a debt her father ran from. Luca Moretti intends to collect, one vow at a time.
Dark, addictive and dangerously romantic, the first book in the Moretti Bratva series.
bio: Sienna Vale writes dark romance for readers who like their heroes morally grey. She lives in Chicago.

title: Ivory & Blood
author: Noor Delacroix
hook: Every queen is a sacrifice. She plans to be the exception.
blurb:
Noor plays chess with the man who ruined her family, and loses on purpose every night.
But each game buys her one more secret, and the board is almost hers. A glamorous, ruthless dark romance where every move costs blood.
bio: Noor Delacroix is a former chess teacher and lifelong reader of villains. She writes from Montreal.

title: Don’t Open It.
author: R. J. Moss
hook: Whatever you hear tonight.
blurb:
Kate's new house is perfect. Except for the door at the end of the hall that the agent said was just a cupboard. Except for the knocking.
She promised her husband she would not open it. But he is not home yet, and the knocking has started to say her name.
bio: R. J. Moss writes psychological thrillers you should not read alone. A former locksmith, Moss lives in a house with no locked doors.

title: The Last Tram
author: Miguel Sarr
hook: Lisbon, 2 a.m. One seat left. Somebody has to die before the last stop.
blurb:
Former agent Rui Sarr takes the last tram home every night. Tonight a stranger hands him a ticket with his old code name on it.
Thirty-one stops. Twelve passengers. One of them is the asset he left for dead in 1999. A taut, elegant spy thriller.
bio: Miguel Sarr spent a decade as a foreign correspondent. He writes thrillers in Lisbon, near the end of the 28 line.

title: Last Night at the Sunny Cove
author: Dana Keller
hook: Check in. Don't check out.
blurb:
The Sunny Cove Motel has nine rooms, one road and no phone signal. Tonight it has eight guests, a dead night manager and a storm that has closed the highway.
Everyone has a reason to be here. Only one has a reason to stay quiet. A breathless locked-room thriller.
bio: Dana Keller grew up in her parents' roadside motel and still sleeps with the light on. Last Night at the Sunny Cove is her third thriller.

title: Fresh Snow
author: J. R. Halden
hook: The snow covered everything. Except the tracks.
blurb:
A car on a frozen lake. One set of footprints leading away. DI Hannah Lowe has six hours before the next snowfall erases the only evidence she has.
The first case in a gripping new detective series.
bio: J. R. Halden is a former police search adviser. The Fresh Snow series is set in the hills where Halden grew up.

title: She Stayed the Night
author: Claire Morrow
layout: giant author + title, one lit window
hook: You invited her in.
blurb:
The storm knocked out the power, and the woman at the door had nowhere else to go. One night, Emma told her husband. Just one.
By morning the guest knows the code to the safe, the name of their son's school and the thing Emma did ten years ago.
bio: Claire Morrow writes domestic thrillers about the people we let too close. She lives in Surrey with her family and a very good alarm.

title: The Breaking of Asterhold
author: K. R. Vael
hook: The mountain kept the empire safe for a thousand years. Last night it moved.
blurb:
When the wardstone of Asterhold cracks, Kael, a disgraced map-maker, is the only one who knows the mountain was never stone at all.
An epic fantasy of storms, old gods and the people too small to be noticed by either. The Ashen Throne, Book One.
bio: K. R. Vael writes epic fantasy and draws the maps first. This is the opening volume of The Ashen Throne.

title: The Crow Thief
author: Mara Leigh
tagline: Every secret has a price. She steals them all.
hook: Every secret has a price. She steals them all.
blurb:
In the city of Varn, secrets are currency and Wren is its finest thief. She has stolen a duke's affair, a priest's doubt and a queen's real name.
Now someone has stolen hers. A dark, glittering fantasy heist.
bio: Mara Leigh writes dark fantasy and keeps a tame crow called Pinch. She lives in Edinburgh.

title: The Drowned Fleet
author: Elias Thorne
tagline: The sea does not keep the dead. It sends them home.
hook: The sea does not keep the dead. It sends them home.
blurb:
Two hundred years after the Drowned Fleet sank, its ships are sailing back into harbour, crewed by sailors who remember everything.
Harbour pilot Isla Thorne must guide them in, and discover what they came back for. A haunting nautical fantasy.
bio: Elias Thorne was raised in a lighthouse family on the Northumbrian coast. He writes fantasy rooted in sea-lore.

title: The Eighth Sphere
author: Lucan Mire
hook: Beyond the seven heavens there is one more. Nobody who sees it comes back the same.
blurb:
Florence, 1467. An engraver's apprentice is asked to finish a deck of cards that maps the universe. The last card, the Eighth Sphere, must be engraved from life.
A literary fantasy about art, astronomy and the cost of seeing too much.
bio: Lucan Mire studied the history of science before turning to fiction. He lives in Bologna.

title: Red Sky Protocol
author: Priya Anand
tagline: Sol 412. The rover is still sending pictures.
hook: Sol 412. The rover is still sending pictures.
blurb:
The crew of Ares Base stopped answering three days ago. Mission controller Priya Anand has only the rover's camera, a twenty-minute signal delay and a sky turning the wrong colour.
A tense, brilliant Mars thriller told one photo at a time.
bio: Priya Anand is a planetary scientist turned novelist. Red Sky Protocol is her first book.

title: Ringfall
author: Jonah Vey
tagline: The rings are coming down. Six days to get everyone off.
hook: The rings are coming down. Six days to get everyone off.
blurb:
For three hundred years humanity lived on the rings of Kepler-9. Now they are falling.
One overworked evacuation officer, one stolen freighter and twelve thousand people who refuse to leave. A big-hearted space opera.
bio: Jonah Vey writes space opera and teaches physics to teenagers who ask better questions than he does.

title: Terminator Line
author: Sam Okoye
tagline: Night falls on the station every 92 minutes. This time it doesn’t lift.
hook: Night falls every 92 minutes. This time it doesn't lift.
blurb:
On the orbital station Meridian, night is a line you cross sixteen times a day. Then the station stops turning toward the sun.
Engineer Ama Okoye has one orbit to find out who did it, and why the ground has gone silent.
bio: Sam Okoye worked on satellite systems for fifteen years. Terminator Line is his debut novel.

title: The Watching Dark
author: Ada Kessler
hook: Something out there has opened its eye.
blurb:
The deep-space telescope Argus was built to see the beginning of time. Instead it has found something looking back.
A chilling space horror novel for readers who like their stars cold and their silences loud.
bio: Ada Kessler is an astrophysicist who writes horror at night. She is not allowed to name the telescope she works on.

title: What the Snow Keeps
author: Rowan Pike
hook: The snow comes early in Harlow. It keeps what it takes.
blurb:
Every winter in Harlow someone walks into the snow and does not come back. In spring, they do.
Mara has waited eleven winters for her brother. This year she means to follow him. A quiet, terrifying novel of grief and white silence.
bio: Rowan Pike writes quiet horror from a cabin in Vermont, where it snows from October to May.

title: The Thing Above the Bed
author: Harlan Voss
hook: Don't look up.
blurb:
Every night since she moved into her grandmother's house, Clara has felt it watching from the ceiling. Every night, it is a little closer.
A gothic horror novel about inheritance, old houses and the things we carry into the dark.
bio: Harlan Voss writes gothic horror and collects nineteenth-century lithographs of things nobody should collect.

title: Beneath Still Water
author: Wren Calloway
hook: The lake has been quiet for forty years. It was waiting.
blurb:
When the reservoir is drained for repairs, the drowned village beneath it rises into the light: church, school, and one house with its lamp still burning.
A creeping gothic novel of what lies under calm water.
bio: Wren Calloway grew up beside a flooded valley in Wales. Beneath Still Water is her second novel.

title: Move-In Ready
author: Dana Whitlock
hook: Freshly painted. Fully furnished. Already occupied.
blurb:
The house was a steal. Mint green, perfect lawn, an open door at the end of the hall that was never on the plans.
A sharp, unsettling haunted-house novel about the price of the perfect home.
bio: Dana Whitlock is a former estate agent. She has seen things in show homes she will not discuss.

title: What the Fields Want
author: Agnes Harrow
layout: single eerie object on pale field
hook: The harvest has always been generous. Someone has always paid.
blurb:
Ellen returns to her mother's farm for one last harvest and finds the old crown hanging in the barn, freshly polished.
The village is very glad to see her. They have been waiting. A folk horror novel steeped in wheat, ritual and dread.
bio: Agnes Harrow writes folk horror from the English fens, where the fields are wider than the sky.

title: The Summer of the Comet
author: Leila Haddad
tagline: It comes back every 6,800 years. She only needs it to come back once.
hook: It comes back every 6,800 years. She only needs it to come back once.
blurb:
The summer the comet crosses the sky, Laila meets a boy who says he has seen it before.
A luminous, heartbreaking YA romance about time, first love and the one night that could change both.
bio: Leila Haddad writes YA romance and stays up for every meteor shower. She lives in Toronto.

title: The Glass Trials
author: Nia Rowe
tagline: Only one of us walks out whole.
hook: Only one of us walks out whole.
blurb:
Every year the glass city chooses twelve. Every year, one comes back.
Nia has trained her whole life to be the one. She didn't plan on the boy who wants to save them all. A breathless YA fantasy.
bio: Nia Rowe writes YA fantasy about girls who refuse to break. She lives in Manchester.

title: Lane Seven
author: Corey Lin
tagline: Someone drowned at the championship. Four hundred people were watching.
hook: Someone drowned at the championship. Four hundred people were watching.
blurb:
Lane Seven belonged to the fastest swimmer in the state. Now she is dead, and the only witness is the girl in Lane Six.
A gripping YA thriller where every teammate has a motive and every second counts.
bio: Corey Lin swam competitively for eight years. Lane Seven is Corey's first novel.

title: Out by Morning
author: June Park
hook: Two exes. One car. A thousand miles to say goodbye.
blurb:
June and Theo broke up in March. In July, a road trip they planned together is the only way to get June's grandmother's ashes home.
A funny, aching YA road-trip novel about letting go.
bio: June Park writes YA from Seoul and Los Angeles and has driven Route 66 twice.

title: The Seventh Trial
author: Juno Hart
layout: emblem on black, single spot colour
hook: Only one may rise.
blurb:
Seven trials. Seven chances to earn a place among the Ascendant. Juno has passed six by cheating.
The seventh cannot be cheated. A propulsive YA dystopian fantasy.
bio: Juno Hart writes YA fantasy and once failed her driving test seven times.

title: The Keeper’s Storm
author: Fern Abbott
hook: The light must never go out.
blurb:
When a winter storm traps eleven-year-old Fern in her grandfather's lighthouse, she learns the light has never gone out in two hundred years.
Tonight the bulb is failing, a ship is coming and Grandad is missing. A thrilling middle-grade adventure.
bio: Fern Abbott grew up on the Scottish coast and still counts the seconds between lighthouse flashes.

title: Kid vs. Bot
author: Sam Ito
tagline: The science fair. The robot. The rematch.
hook: The science fair. The robot. The rematch.
blurb:
Sam's robot lost last year's science fair to a toaster. This year Sam has built something better. Too much better.
Now the robot wants to win the fair, the school and maybe the town. A laugh-out-loud STEM comedy.
bio: Sam Ito is a robotics engineer and a former science fair loser.

title: The Map Under the Floorboards
author: Toby Marsh
hook: X marks the spot. The spot is under your bed.
blurb:
When Toby's floorboard creaks for the hundredth time, he finally pries it up and finds a map of his own street, a hundred years old, with one house marked in red.
A treasure hunt across one ordinary neighbourhood, full of extraordinary secrets.
bio: Toby Marsh writes adventure stories in an old house with very creaky floors.

title: Ollie Vance Is Not a Spy
author: Rita Clarke
hook: He's definitely not a spy. Probably.
blurb:
Ollie Vance is eleven, terrible at secrets and the only kid who saw the headmaster bury a suitcase.
Now everyone thinks he is a spy, including the actual spies. A fast, funny mystery for anyone who has ever been in the wrong place at the right time.
bio: Rita Clarke writes funny books for clever kids. She is not a spy.

title: The Cat Saw Everything
author: Winifred Ames
hook: Mrs. Peabody's cat was the only witness. Luckily, she speaks cat.
blurb:
When the vicar is found in the rose garden, the village blames the gardener. Mrs. Peabody blames no one until her cat has had his say.
A charming golden-age cozy mystery, the first of the series.
bio: Winifred Ames writes cozy mysteries with a cat on her lap and a pot of tea always cooling.

title: Foxglove & Fruitcake
author: Daisy Harrow
hook: A pinch of poison. A slice of cake. A village full of suspects.
blurb:
Daisy's prize-winning fruitcake is the last thing the judge ate. Now Lavender Lane wants to know who added the foxglove.
A delicious garden cozy, the first Lavender Lane Mystery.
bio: Daisy Harrow grows foxgloves and bakes far too much. She has never poisoned anyone.

title: Shortbread and Shallow Graves
author: Bea Marlowe
hook: The secret ingredient was murder.
blurb:
Bea's bakery is famous for one thing: shortbread so good it should be illegal. Then the town councillor dies with crumbs on his lips.
The first Thistle Bay Bakery Mystery, with recipes.
bio: Bea Marlowe runs a seaside tea room in her daydreams and writes cozies in real life.

title: A Stitch Too Far
author: Polly Greer
hook: Knit one. Purl one. Find the killer.
blurb:
The Knit & Natter circle meets every Tuesday. This Tuesday, one member is missing, and her half-finished scarf spells out a name.
A warm, witty craft cozy, the first Knit & Natter Mystery.
bio: Polly Greer has knitted 200 scarves and plotted 20 murders. Only one of those is a hobby.

title: Where Are You Going, Bear?
author: Holly Penn
hook: Bear has packed his suitcase. But where is he going?
blurb:
Bear is ready for a big adventure. He has a hat, a snack and a very small suitcase.
A gentle, funny picture book about growing up, saying goodbye and finding your way home.
bio: Holly Penn writes picture books for her nieces, who are tough critics.

title: Little Whale, Big Sea
author: Mo Delaney
hook: The sea is very big. Little Whale is very small.
blurb:
Little Whale wants to see the whole sea. The sea is very big. But friends make big things smaller.
A warm cut-paper picture book about courage and curiosity.
bio: Mo Delaney makes picture books with scissors, glue and a lot of blue paper.

title: Ten Yellow Raincoats
author: Pip Larkin
hook: Ten yellow raincoats. One red one.
blurb:
Count the yellow raincoats as they splash to school. But one raincoat is red, and it is going the other way.
A bright counting picture book about fitting in and standing out.
bio: Pip Larkin writes and draws picture books on rainy days, which in Manchester is most days.

title: Goodnight, Small Fox
author: Ana Ruiz
hook: The moon is up. The hills are quiet. Small Fox is almost asleep.
blurb:
Small Fox says goodnight to the hills, the stars and the very big moon.
A soothing bedtime picture book to read again and again.
bio: Ana Ruiz writes bedtime stories in Seville and reads them to her twins every night.

title: Her Hands Knew
author: Dolores Reyes
tagline: A memoir of my grandmother’s kitchen
hook: My grandmother never wrote down a recipe. Her hands remembered for her.
blurb:
Dolores Reyes spent her childhood at her grandmother's elbow in a Oaxacan kitchen. Decades later, with her grandmother gone, she sets out to rebuild every dish from memory.
A memoir of food, family and the knowledge that lives in our hands.
bio: Dolores Reyes is a food writer and teacher in Los Angeles. This is her first book.

title: The Night Desk
author: Paul Brennan
tagline: Thirty years on the city beat
hook: Thirty years on the city beat. Every story true.
blurb:
For three decades Paul Brennan worked the night desk of a city newspaper, the man who took the call when the world went wrong at 3 a.m.
A vivid, funny and moving memoir of a vanished trade.
bio: Paul Brennan was a crime and night news editor for thirty years. He now sleeps at night.

title: Two Rivers Home
author: Amara Nwosu
hook: One river carried her away. The other brought her home.
blurb:
Amara Nwosu left Onitsha at nineteen and built a life in Glasgow. At fifty she went back to the Niger with her mother's ashes and a list of questions.
A luminous memoir of two homes and the water between them.
bio: Amara Nwosu is a Nigerian-Scottish writer and radio presenter.

title: Above the Weather
author: Sam Ortega
subtitle: A Memoir of Mountains, Grief, and Coming Home
layout: vast landscape, tiny figure, bold sans
hook: At 8,000 metres you learn who you really are.
blurb:
Sam Ortega climbed Everest to prove something to his father. He came down with something else entirely.
A thrilling, honest memoir of altitude, failure and forgiveness.
bio: Sam Ortega is a mountaineer and photographer. He has stood on four of the seven summits.

title: The Kitchen Table Years
author: Rosa Delgado
hook: Everything important happened at the kitchen table.
blurb:
Births announced, letters read, bills argued over, cakes cut. Rosa Delgado's family lived its whole life around one wooden table.
A warm, funny memoir of a house, a family and the table that held them together.
bio: Rosa Delgado writes essays about food and family. She still has the table.

title: a crow, a plum, a moon
author: haruka sato
hook: haiku for the in-between hours
bio: haruka sato writes haiku in Kyoto and on long train rides. this is her first collection.
excerpt:
a crow on the branch —
the plum has not decided
whether to fall yet

title: every flower i kept
author: cara linden
hook: poems about keeping and letting go
bio: cara linden writes poetry about love, loss and gardens. she lives in Portland.
excerpt:
i pressed every flower you gave me
between the pages of books i never finished.
now the books are mostly flowers.

title: what we let fly
author: eli brandt
hook: poems
bio: eli brandt is a poet and birdwatcher in the Scottish Highlands.
excerpt:
we opened our hands
and called it losing.
the birds called it the sky.

title: salt, then sweetness
author: noor rahimi
hook: poems of heartbreak and healing
bio: noor rahimi is an Afghan-American poet. salt, then sweetness is her second collection.
excerpt:
first the salt,
the tears you swore you would not cry.
then, slowly, the sweetness,
like lemons left out in the sun.

title: what the light forgave
author: elias rowe
hook: poems
bio: elias rowe writes and photographs in Lisbon.
excerpt:
the light came in anyway,
through the curtain,
through everything i did not say.

title: Stop Shrinking.
author: Jade Monroe
tagline: How to take up space without apology
hook: You were never too much.
blurb: Women are taught to take up less space: lower voices, smaller asks, quieter ambitions. Jade Monroe spent twenty years shrinking until she couldn't breathe.
bio: Jade Monroe is a leadership coach and speaker. She has helped thousands of women stop apologising.
bullets: Why we shrink, and what it costs us
Scripts for asking for more, without apology
A 30-day plan to take up space at work and at home

title: Do Less, Better.
author: Nate Calder
tagline: The quiet power of doing fewer things, well.
hook: The quiet power of doing fewer things, well.
blurb: You don't need a better to-do list. You need a shorter one.
bio: Nate Calder is a productivity researcher and former consultant. He now works four days a week.
bullets: The three-question test that cuts any list in half
How to say no without guilt
A one-page weekly system that actually sticks

title: The Quiet Yes
author: Mira Shah
tagline: How to say yes to what matters, and no to everything else
hook: Say yes to what matters. And no to everything else.
blurb: Every yes is a no to something else. Mira Shah shows how to choose your yeses on purpose.
bio: Mira Shah is a psychologist and coach. She lives in London and says no to most meetings.
bullets: Find the yes that fits your values
Turn down requests kindly and clearly
Build a calendar that feels like your own

title: The Small Company Advantage
author: Tom Avery
tagline: Why ten people beat ten thousand
hook: Why ten people beat ten thousand.
blurb: The best companies are not the biggest. They are the most focused.
bio: Tom Avery founded three small companies and sold none of them on purpose.
bullets: Why small teams move faster and think better
How to grow profit without growing headcount
Case studies from twelve firms under 50 people

title: One Thing Fully
author: Marcus Hale
subtitle: The Art of Focus in a World That Won't Stop
layout: white, huge type, one small graphic
hook: Stop multitasking. Start living.
blurb: We do everything at once and nothing well. This book shows a better way.
bio: Marcus Hale is a writer and teacher on focus and attention. He lives in Colorado.
bullets: The science of attention, in plain words
How to protect one hour a day for what matters

title: Hands Open
author: Daniel Asante
hook: When you don't know what to pray, open your hands.
blurb: For the seasons of loss, waiting and doubt, Daniel Asante offers short prayers and honest reflections drawn from the Psalms.
bio: Daniel Asante is a pastor in Birmingham and a father of three.
bullets: Reflections on the Psalms of lament

title: Keep the Lamp Lit
author: Simon Hale
hook: Prayers for the long night.
blurb: For the hours when sleep won't come and worry will, these short prayers keep a light burning.
bio: Simon Hale is a hospital chaplain who has sat through many long nights.
bullets: Night prayers for every day of the month

title: Pages of Morning
author: Ruth Collins
tagline: A year of short readings for the first ten minutes
hook: A year of short readings for the first ten minutes.
blurb: Before the phone, before the news, one page. Ruth Collins offers a reading, a verse and a question for every morning of the year.
bio: Ruth Collins writes devotionals and teaches Bible study in Nashville.
bullets: A verse and a reflection question each day
A reading plan through the Gospels

title: Still Water Mornings
author: Grace Whitfield
hook: Be still, and know.
blurb: Forty short devotions for anxious hearts, each one a quiet place to rest before the day begins.
bio: Grace Whitfield is a writer and counsellor who has lived with anxiety and found peace.
bullets: A breath prayer for every day

title: The Footprint
author: Martin Hale
tagline: Apollo 11 and the eight days that changed what we thought was possible
hook: Eight days that changed what we thought was possible.
blurb: July 1969. Three men, one fragile spacecraft and a footprint that will outlast them all. Drawing on new interviews and archives, Martin Hale tells the story of Apollo 11 hour by hour.
bio: Martin Hale is a historian of science and spaceflight. He lives in Houston.
bullets: The launch, landing and return, minute by minute
What the Moon landing still means

title: Silver Owls
author: Helena Pappas
hook: How one coin built Athens.
blurb: The silver owl of Athens paid for a navy, a temple and a democracy. Helena Pappas follows the coin from mine to market to empire.
bio: Helena Pappas is a historian of the ancient economy and teaches in Athens.
bullets: The Laurion silver mines and the people who worked them
The owl's journey across the ancient world

title: The Wight Gale
author: Rupert Coyle
tagline: The storm that broke a fleet, 1795
hook: The storm that broke a fleet, 1795.
blurb: In November 1795 a hurricane-force gale struck the British fleet off the Isle of Wight. Hundreds died in a single night.
bio: Rupert Coyle is a maritime historian and sailor on the Solent.
bullets: The night of the storm, ship by ship
The sailors, wives and children aboard
How the disaster changed naval history

title: The Bridge at Dawn
author: James Thornbury
subtitle: Seventy Hours That Decided the War in the West
hook: One bridge. One morning. The war in the balance.
blurb: At dawn on 7 March 1945, American soldiers found a bridge across the Rhine still standing. The next ten hours changed the end of the war.
bio: James Thornbury is a military historian and former army officer.
bullets: The race for the Rhine, hour by hour

title: Emperors of Sand
author: Helena Marsh
subtitle: Rome's Desert Frontier and the Fall of an Empire
hook: The empires the desert remembered.
